title: 8 years of editing knowledge as Claude skills
summary: Years before AI, I built my own auto-cut tool and edited 7 videos in 7 days. Now that editing knowledge (trimming, pacing, motion design, After Effects) is written down as Claude skills. Two of them are free here, plus a prompt to turn your own know-how into a skill.
steps: For a talking-head video, get a transcript with timestamps, then use Prompt 1.
For screen recordings in After Effects, use Prompt 2.
Write your first own skill with Prompt 3.
The caption fixer skill is on the Day 2 page.

prompts.title: 1. Cut list for my talking-head A-roll
prompts.text:
Use the aroll-trim-pacing rules. Here is my raw talking-head transcript with timestamps: [ATTACH TRANSCRIPT, word-level if possible].
1. Tell me the one-sentence promise of this video. The first 3 seconds must state or show it.
2. Where I repeat a line, keep the last complete, confident take, unless an earlier one has clearly better energy.
3. Cut on silences, never mid-word. Leave 80 to 120 ms of air before and after each line.
4. Remove false starts, filler words and "so, um" openers. Keep a laugh or reaction if it adds personality.
5. Never end mid-sentence. Value first, then the call to action.
Output a cut list table: in, out, line text, reason. Then list moments that need B-roll, a punch-in or a graphic (at least every 4 seconds), with timestamps.
Do not edit my project. This is a plan for me to review.

prompts.title: 2. Screen-recording zooms in After Effects
prompts.text:
Use the screen-recording-zoom-build skill. My screen recording is [FILE NAME], [3840x2160], and it is in [PATH TO PROJECT.aep].
Moments to show: [LIST: time, what to zoom on, highlight or lower third text]
1. Save a backup of the project first.
2. Keep the comp at the source size. Write one helper .jsx with frame(window), addRect and setKeys.
3. Make each beat {start, dur, window:[x,y,w,h], ease}. Zoom gently (max 2.2x), eased, with 0.4 s hold after each move. Never show the edge of the recording.
4. Highlights: rounded rectangles that keep the same stroke width while zooming. Lower thirds: title plus subline, 0.3 s fade or slide, inside title-safe.
5. Render a still at every beat, check framing, text and safe areas, fix problems and re-run.
Tell me what you built and which beats I should check by eye.

prompts.title: 3. Turn my editing know-how into a Claude skill
prompts.text:
I want to turn one thing I do well as an editor into a Claude skill: [e.g. "how I pace a 30-second reel" / "how I pick B-roll" / "how I name and sort footage"].
Interview me with 6 to 8 questions, one at a time: what goes in, the exact steps, my rules that must never break, common mistakes, and what the finished output looks like.
Then write a SKILL.md with:
- a top block with name: (lowercase-with-dashes) and description: (what it does and when to use it)
- sections: Inputs, Rules, Steps, Output, Never
Keep it short and specific. Then tell me where to save it: ~/.claude/skills/[NAME]/SKILL.md

notes: Skills hold your rules. You still review the cut and the final edit.
